prompt.context: Athletic Athleisure (AA) is a boutique, high-end athletic apparel brand that is considering acquiring Vinyasapp, an app-based yoga and Pilates platform. The app has been performing very well over the past two years, so the management team at Vinyasapp is willing to sell for $50M. AA has strong brand recognition and enjoys a positive reputation in its industry. The wellness industry has grown exponentially in recent years, as individuals have become more concerned about their health and are exploring more convenient ways to exercise. AA's customers are very loyal to its brand and its main customers are individuals who practice yoga and Pilates regularly. Their products include compression and moisture-wicking workout attire and accessories. Their customers are generally technologically savvy and would be interested in taking virtual workout classes. In recent quarters, AA has experienced a decline in profitability due to supply chain constraints and an increase in fixed operating costs from keeping large stores open. They are considering closing down some of their brick-and-mortar locations in favor of selling more of their products online.
prompt.question: Should Athletic Athleisure purchase Vinyasapp for $50M? AA's CEO wants to reverse the trend in profitability and hopes to add $8M in annual EBITDA over the next 3 years.

clarifying_info.q: What is AA's current EBITDA or profitability level?
clarifying_info.a: The case does not specify current EBITDA; the goal is to add $8M in annual EBITDA over the next 3 years.

clarifying_info.q: How is AA considering financing the acquisition?
clarifying_info.a: Financing structure is not specified; candidate should consider cash, debt, or equity options.

clarifying_info.q: Does AA have any existing digital or app capabilities?
clarifying_info.a: AA does not have existing app development expertise.

clarifying_info.q: What is Vinyasapp's current user base or growth rate?
clarifying_info.a: The app has been performing very well over the past two years; refer to market data exhibit when provided.

exhibits.title: Yoga App Market Size
exhibits.shows: A bar chart of total yoga app market size in $M from 2018 to 2022, alongside a 2022 market share breakdown by app competitor showing six named players and their percentage shares.

exhibits.title: Vinyasapp 2022 Operating Expenses
exhibits.shows: A bar chart of Vinyasapp's 2022 operating expenses broken into four line items in $M.

exhibits.title: Recent Sports & Recreation App Acquisitions
exhibits.shows: A table of five recent comparable app acquisitions showing company name, description, EBITDA, and selling price.

framework: Market: assess the size, growth, and competitive dynamics of the yoga app market
Target Company: evaluate Vinyasapp's revenue, profitability, product, and customer base
Synergies: identify branding, revenue growth, and cost reduction opportunities from combining AA and Vinyasapp
Capabilities & Risks: assess AA's technical expertise gaps, management bandwidth, labor attrition from potential store closures, and marketing capability
Financing / Deal Economics: evaluate cash, debt, or equity financing and the impact on AA's EBITDA target

questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply Vinyasapp's 2022 market share by total 2022 market size. Strong candidates note the market is growing at ~11% YoY and that Vinyasapp is the largest single player.

math.setup: Revenue = Market Share % x Total Market Size = 18% x $278M

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate Vinyasapp's 2022 total operating expenses and EBITDA.
questions.guidance: Candidate should sum all four operating expense line items, then subtract from revenue. Strong candidates flag that App Development is the largest cost at 18/44 = ~41% of opex, note potential to cut but caution against doing so given competitive market dynamics.

math.setup: Total OpEx = Cost of Revenue + App Development + G&A + Marketing & Sales; EBITDA = Revenue - Total OpEx

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, estimate the enterprise value of Vinyasapp using the comparable transactions method.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate the EBITDA multiple (Selling Price / EBITDA) for each comparable, exclude Expansion Equipment as non-comparable (it is a physical goods marketplace, not a fitness app), average the remaining four multiples, and apply to Vinyasapp's EBITDA. Candidate should articulate why Expansion Equipment is excluded.

math.setup: Multiple = Selling Price / EBITDA for each comp; exclude non-comparable; average remaining; apply to Vinyasapp EBITDA
steps: Expansion Equipment: 253 / 23 = 11x — EXCLUDE (not a fitness app)
math.answer: Implied EV = ~$48M; $50M asking price is close to fair value at ~8.3x EBITDA

brainstorming.prompt: What should the client consider about expanding into the wellness app space? What are some possible advantages or disadvantages of this expansion strategy?

categories.name: Opportunities
ideas: Entry point into a lucrative and growing wellness app industry
Diversifies AA's business model away from traditional brick-and-mortar retail
AA's current yoga and Pilates customers are a natural and ready-made user base for Vinyasapp
Supports AA's strategic shift toward online sales channels
Brand halo effect: premium AA brand could elevate Vinyasapp's perception and pricing power

categories.name: Challenges & Risks
ideas: AA lacks expertise in app development, creating dependency on Vinyasapp talent retention
Significant marketing spend likely needed to grow Vinyasapp's user base, pressuring EBITDA targets
AA's customers may already be loyal to competing yoga app platforms, raising customer acquisition costs
Little operational overlap between apparel retail and app development complicates synergy realization
Vinyasapp's $6M EBITDA falls short of the $8M annual EBITDA target without additional cost cuts or synergies

recommendation: Recommend that AA move forward with the acquisition of Vinyasapp
Vinyasapp is the largest player in a growing yoga app market and generates ~$6M in EBITDA at an implied 8x multiple
The $50M asking price is roughly in line with comparable transaction values (~$48M implied), making the deal fairly priced
The acquisition supports AA's strategic pivot away from brick-and-mortar and toward online channels, and AA's loyal yoga/Pilates customer base is a natural fit for Vinyasapp
risks: The $6M EBITDA from Vinyasapp alone does not fully meet the CEO's $8M annual EBITDA target; synergies or cost-cutting initiatives must be identified
AA has no app development expertise, creating key-person and execution risk
Limited operational overlap between apparel retail and a digital platform may make achieving synergies difficult and slow
AA's existing customers may already be committed to other yoga app platforms, increasing customer acquisition costs
next_steps: Identify specific cost-cutting opportunities within Vinyasapp's $44M opex base (particularly App Development at $18M) that can bridge the gap to $8M EBITDA without compromising competitiveness
Develop a retention plan for Vinyasapp's engineering and product talent post-acquisition
Assess financing structure (cash vs. debt vs. equity) and model impact on AA's overall EBITDA and balance sheet
Map AA's customer database against Vinyasapp's user base to quantify cross-sell opportunity and estimate customer acquisition costs
